title: Control severe external bleeding
immediate_action: Apply direct pressure to the wound with a clean cloth
If bleeding soaks through, add more dressings — do not remove original
If bleeding continues, apply a tourniquet proximal to wound and note time
expanded_steps: Use gloves if available to protect yourself
Maintain firm, steady pressure for at least 10 minutes
Elevate the injured limb above heart level if possible
For tourniquet: Place 2-3 inches above wound, tighten until bleeding stops
warnings: Do NOT remove embedded objects from the wound
Do NOT release tourniquet once applied
Do NOT apply tourniquet over a joint
no_tool_fallback: Use any clean cloth, clothing, or bare hands for pressure
failure_fallback: Maintain pressure and evacuate to definitive care immediately
source_reference: Field Medical Guide v2.1, Chapter 4, Pages 12-15

title: Perform CPR on unresponsive adult
immediate_action: Call for emergency help or have someone call
Begin chest compressions: 30 compressions at 100-120/min, 2 inches deep
Give 2 rescue breaths if trained, otherwise continue compressions only
expanded_steps: Place heel of hand on center of chest between nipples
Lock elbows and use body weight for compressions
Allow full chest recoil between compressions
Continue 30:2 cycle until help arrives or patient responds
warnings: Do NOT stop compressions for more than 10 seconds
Do NOT compress too slowly or too shallow
Do NOT perform CPR on a person with a pulse
no_tool_fallback: Perform hands-only CPR without rescue breaths
failure_fallback: Continue CPR until help arrives or exhaustion

title: Clear airway obstruction in conscious adult
immediate_action: Stand behind person and wrap arms around waist
Make a fist with one hand and place thumb side against abdomen above navel
Grasp fist with other hand and thrust inward and upward sharply
expanded_steps: Repeat thrusts until object is expelled or person becomes unconscious
If person can cough forcefully, encourage continued coughing
Be prepared to catch person if they lose consciousness
warnings: Do NOT perform abdominal thrusts on infants under 1 year
Do NOT slap the back if person is still able to breathe
Do NOT give up - continue until help arrives
no_tool_fallback: Use Heimlich maneuver with bare hands
failure_fallback: If unconscious, begin CPR and check mouth between compressions
source_reference: Red Cross First Aid Manual 2021, Chapter 8

title: Immobilize suspected fracture
immediate_action: Do not move the injured limb unless absolutely necessary
Apply a splint above and below the injury site
Secure splint with bandages or cloth, not too tight
expanded_steps: Check circulation, sensation, and movement before and after splinting
Pad the splint with soft material for comfort
Elevate the limb if possible to reduce swelling
warnings: Do NOT try to realign the bone
Do NOT apply ice directly to skin
Do NOT move the person if spinal injury is suspected
no_tool_fallback: Use sticks, rolled newspapers, or cardboard as improvised splint
failure_fallback: Support limb in position found and seek immediate medical care

title: Treat moderate to severe burn
immediate_action: Remove person from heat source and stop burning process
Cool the burn with cool (not ice cold) running water for 10-20 minutes
Cover burn with sterile, non-adhesive dressing
expanded_steps: Remove jewelry and tight clothing before swelling occurs
Keep person warm with blanket (not on burned area)
warnings: Do NOT use ice, butter, or ointments on burns
Do NOT break blisters or remove stuck clothing
Do NOT touch the burn with anything unsterile
no_tool_fallback: Use clean cloth or plastic wrap to cover burn
failure_fallback: Keep burn clean and dry, seek medical attention immediately
source_reference: Emergency Care Manual v3.2, Burns Section
